newsitem.title: UK: BOE's George says rates may have to go over 6.0%.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George says rates may have to go over 6.0%.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George advised Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke at the September 23 monetary meeting to raise interest rates by a quarter-point to 6.0 percent and warned that they might have to rise even further.
Minutes of the meeting said George acknowledged that a case could always be made for delaying a rate rise.
"But if the buoyancy of the last month's data was to be confirmed over the five weeks to the next meeting, it might become necessary to tighten policy more sharply," George was quoted as saying.
Official interest rates were left unchanged at 5.75 percent after the meeting, but raised to 6.0 percent after the subsequent meeting on October 30.
George noted that retail price inflation, measured by RPIX, had remained stubbornly at 2.8 percent year on year for the fifth month in a row -- above Clarke's target of 2.5 percent by next April.

"It was not clear exactly why this had happened, but the Bank was now less confident that underlying inflation would in fact fall to within the target over the next few months," the minutes quoted George as saying.
Clarke also expressed surprise that RPI inflation had not so far followed producer prices down, although he said upward revisions to first half GDP made it easier to understand why this was the case.

He said there was evidence that "a reasonable recovery" was underway. The housing market was becoming a little stronger but was by no means remarkable by historical standards and retail sales were becoming "quite strong."
He expected the recovery to continue through the year.
"Any downside risk of a long period of below-trend growth had significantly declined," the minutes quoted Clarke as saying.
Clarke said he saw no signs of inflationary pressures re-emerging and concluded that the case for a rise in interest rates was not yet proven.

"Even after the GDP revisions, output growth was close to, but not above, trend. However, as he had made clear at previous meetings, if the picture changed to a point where the chances were that the inflation target would not be met, he would not hesitate to raise interest rates," the minutes said.
In the discussion, the point was made that RPI inflation might not be falling as swiftly as expected because retailers might be taking advantage of strong demand to raise prices.
Although George advised an immediate rate rise to 6.0 percent, he acknowledged the possibility that the latest economic data were "erratically strong."
He also said that while demand was rather clearly on an upward trend, output may still be held back for a time by further downward stock adjustment.

Finally, the relative strength of sterling, if it persisted, would help to contain any immediate pickup in inflation as a consequence of what he described as "fairly solid further evidence of the gathering economic momentum that the Bank had been projecting for some time."
